attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his newsletter, endorsed.

semantics.note: 'it's now obvious that if it does there will be' is firm conditional language. The antecedent (Microsoft capex dips) is kept. 'Direct effects' is reasonably read as adverse from the context.

contract.note: Counting any sequential dip as meeting the antecedent is a generous reading, since the speaker likely meant a real pullback. The contract partly corrects for this by requiring lease timing to be separated from real investment and by requiring causal evidence. No lag or index is named, so interpretation matters.

evidence.note: Microsoft's own disclosure of a sequential decline in the January–March 2026 quarter, attributed to buildout variability and finance-lease timing. It bears on the antecedent only. It is not evidence of any economic or market effect.

reviews.rationale: A quarterly decline is documented, but it is mostly explained by lease timing. Whether it counts as the 'dip' the speaker meant is debatable. The packet has no evidence linking any effect on US output or the stock market to this decline, and there is no deadline. The forecast cannot be settled on this evidence.

attribution.note: Zitron's own estimate. The Axios figure is attributed to Axios and is not scored.

semantics.note: The period ended before the post, so this is an estimate of past spending and is properly an observation. Setting modality to 'likely' is wrong: under policy, 'I expect' is firm, unqualified expectation, so the claim is scorable.

contract.note: Defining Mag Seven as the seven named firms, the period as calendar H1 2025, and the threshold as more than $200B is an ordinary reading. Because the capex basis (cash vs. lease-inclusive) and fiscal-calendar alignment are unspecified, close results could turn on interpretation.

evidence.note: Meta Q2 2025 capex of about $17B, including finance-lease principal. One quarter for one company, not the seven-company H1 total.
Alphabet Q2 2025 capex of $22.4B. One component only.
NVIDIA's fiscal year differs from the calendar year, so its figures need reconciling. Contains no capex figure.
Apple's fiscal calendar ends in September. Shows only the fiscal-period convention, no figure that bears on the total.

reviews.rationale: The packet gives only two quarterly components and notes on fiscal calendars. It contains no reproducible January–June 2025 total for all seven companies, so it cannot show whether combined capex exceeded $200B.

attribution.note: Zitron's own judgment about Kedrosky's estimate. Kedrosky's figures are quoted and are not the claim.

semantics.note: The claim is that the estimate's method leaves out Oracle and private developers and is therefore too low. It is a contemporaneous assessment of the estimate, and the drafter rightly left out the ambiguous $520B figure.

contract.note: The contract reframes the claim as a forecast and brings back the $520B benchmark, which the normalised claim dropped as ambiguous. It also imposes a US-only AI scope the speaker did not specify. Whether the result is supported depends on these choices, not on the speaker's words.

evidence.note: A secondary account of Kedrosky's $312B method, extrapolated from NVIDIA's sales. If accurate, that method might already capture Oracle and developer purchases indirectly. The original calculation was not verified, so this is context only.
Dell'Oro's worldwide data-center capex growth figures, including growth in Oracle's spending. The scope differs from the claim, and it says nothing about what Kedrosky's estimate included.

reviews.rationale: The packet does not establish which estimate is meant or whether its method excluded Oracle and private developers. A secondary report hints that it may have captured them through NVIDIA sales, but the original method could not be checked. No comparable spending total settles whether the estimate was too low.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his newsletter, endorsed.

semantics.note: The 'doesn't seem' hedge is correctly kept. The core proposition, not close to profitability, is phrased as an impression rather than a firm assertion.

contract.note: The contract itself says 'doesn't seem' expresses uncertainty, yet it scores the claim on a plain reading. Policy allows plain readings only for firm language. 'Close to profitable' also has no threshold or accounting basis.

evidence.note: Digiday, citing The Information: about $65M of cash burn against $34M of revenue in 2024. This is an earlier period and cash-based, not net income for the target quarter.
Sacra's estimate of $100M ARR in March 2025. An annualized revenue estimate that says nothing about earnings.

reviews.rationale: The scored element is hedged ('doesn't seem'), and hedged language is not scored under policy. Even on a firm reading, the packet has no company-wide earnings for Q2 2025, only 2024 cash burn and an ARR estimate.
